title: Salted caramel truffles
subtitle: A caramel ganache centre with a flake of sea salt, coated in dark chocolate
excerpt: Salted caramel truffles combine a smooth dark caramel ganache with a finish of fine sea salt. The caramel is made first, cream added to arrest the cooking, then dark chocolate is melted in to produce a dense, silky filling. Each truffle is set with a coating of tempered dark chocolate and finished with a small flake of salt.
sourceNotes: Salted caramel confectionery is associated with Henri Le Roux, who popularised the caramel au beurre salé at his chocolaterie in Quiberon, Brittany. The combination of salted caramel filling with dark chocolate became standard across fine chocolateries.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze on a tray in a single layer, then transfer to a box for up to 2 months. Defrost in the fridge overnight.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Make up to 5 days ahead. Refrigerate in a single layer in an airtight container.

glossaryTerms.definition: A ganache where caramelised sugar is made first and cream added to the hot caramel before chocolate is stirred in. The result is richer and more complex than a plain cream-and-chocolate ganache.

content.text: centre enclosed in a thin coating of dark chocolate. The sea salt is added in two places: a pinch in the ganache for flavour and a small flake on the outside for contrast. If hot syrup touches skin, run cold water over it for at least ten minutes and seek medical care if needed.

Cook 150 g caster sugar in a dry pan to a deep amber caramel, 175°C. Remove from the heat and immediately pour in the warmed cream, it will bubble violently. Stir until smooth. Add the butter and stir until glossy. Pour the hot caramel over 100 g chopped dark chocolate. Stir until smooth. Add a pinch of sea salt flakes. Pour into a shallow dish and refrigerate for 1 hour until firm enough to roll.

Scoop the firm ganache into small rounds and roll into balls between cold palms. Place on a lined tray and refrigerate until firm. Melt 200 g dark chocolate over a barely simmering pan of water, then cool to 31°C (tempered, glossy and slightly thick). Using a fork, dip each ganache ball into the chocolate, allow the excess to drain, and place on a lined tray. Immediately drop a single flake of sea salt on top before the coating sets.
